column1: The Emotional Brain|1996|0|0||7.5,6.5,7,8,7.5,7.5,5,9,8,7.5|Joseph E. LeDoux|Research-based explanation of emotional processing, learning and neural pathways; not a neuropsychology training manual. https://www.simonandschuster.com/books/The-Emotional-Brain/Joseph-Ledoux/9780684836591 describes mechanisms and supplies specialist review extracts; https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/nlmcatalog/9704030 verifies original 1996 and references 335–372 of 384 pages. Treat this as a historical stage of the research program, not a complete current account of consciousness or emotion. D=7.5 low confidence from contents and review extracts; distinct experiments add learning, elementary brain exposition may be lower-yield. Disease examples are applications rather than dominant topic; no T11/T12 or historical-period deduction.

Descartes's Error|1994|0|0||7,7,7.5,7.5,7.5,8,5.5,9,8,8|Antonio R. Damasio|Explanatory argument linking bodily emotion and decision-making, not a clinical curriculum. https://www.loc.gov/item/94028473/ verifies 1994 and references 269–297 of 312 pages. The somatic-marker hypothesis is not treated as settled: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/16197997/ identifies ambiguity in psychophysiological interpretation and limited causal evidence. That warrants cautious E, not automatic V1 for an explicitly proposed scientific hypothesis. D=7.5 low confidence from structure and scholarly discussion; lesion cases add distinctions, whole-book pacing unverified. Neurological cases support a general account, so disease does not predominate. Philosophy is framing around neuroscience rather than the central domain; no T12, H13=0.

The Tangled Wing|1982|0|0||7.5,8,6.5,7,7,8,5.5,9,7.5,8|Melvin Konner|Integrative behavioral biology connecting physiology, development, anthropology and culture. General explanatory synthesis rather than a technical reference despite breadth. https://www.melvinkonner.com/the-tangled-wing/ distinguishes 1982 original from complete 2002 revision; https://ishe.org/wp-content/uploads/2019/11/HEB_2002_17_2_1-27.pdf supplies specialist review of revised edition. Assessment benefits from revised-edition evidence but P14 remains 1982. D=7 low confidence: many subfields provide distinct learning; expansive literary and social discussion may have lower yield. No central disease/ecology theme established and no thematic deduction from peripheral policy conclusions. Timeless human-behavior argument H13=0.

Evolving the Mind|1996|0|10||6,7,5.5,5.5,6.5,6.5,6.5,7.5,7,7|A.G. Cairns-Smith|Accessible conceptual exploration from matter to nerves and consciousness, with speculative quantum mechanisms. https://openlibrary.org/books/OL1113466M/Evolving_the_mind verifies 1996, purpose and references 299–315 of 329 numbered pages. https://philpapers.org/rec/DENROC documents Dennett's critical response; the proposed quantum explanation should not be treated as established. No evidence inspected establishes deliberate or central concealed certainty sufficient for V1. D=6.5 low confidence from description, sample and review discussion; familiar physics may add little for this reader, biological transitions add distinctions. T12 philosophy of consciousness, H13=0.

A History of the Mind|1992|0|10||6.5,6.5,5.5,6,7,7.5,5.5,8.5,8,7.5|Nicholas Humphrey|Evolutionary argument about sensation and subjective experience using blindsight and phantom-limb cases, not a chronological textbook despite the title. https://link.springer.com/book/9780387987194 verifies original 1992 and distinguishes 1999 reprint. Hypothesis remains a proposal rather than a demonstrated solution to consciousness, limiting E and M. D=7 low-confidence description/contents estimate: distinct dissociations add learning, overall causal synthesis less secure. T12 philosophy of mind; clinical examples do not make disease predominant. H13=0 for evolutionary explanation. https://wellcomecollection.org/works/h5bra2b6 documents 1999 edition, 238 pages and bibliography 229–234.
